body:
> if I `source ~/.zshrc` then it starts happening

Why source `.zshrc` manually? What are you trying to do? Most likely you should put them (excluding Starship initialization, of course) into a function and execute that instead.

> so maybe the bug is related to when `eval "$(starship init zsh)"` is run a second time?

True, possibly due to `zle reset-prompt` being called twice.

> #### Expected Behavior
> No lines should be "eaten" when entering and leaving vi mode

I would say that *is* expected behavior, since the shell config is mangled.

Closing as this is not a bug in Starship, but feel free to continue the discussion.

Hi @kidonng thanks for replying :)

> Why source .zshrc manually?

I use tmux, and when I update something in my `zshrc` (e.g. adding an env var) I run a script to source `zshrc` in all my tmux windows to get the change to my config. I would have assumed needing to resource `zshrc` because you needed to change some config isn't that uncommon?

> True, possibly due to zle reset-prompt being called twice.

Is there some way to maybe wrap `eval "$(starship init zsh)"` in a guard so that it isn't called a second time?

> I would say that is expected behavior, since the shell config is mangled.

I would say that it is a bug with starship, because I've never had this issue with any other prompt that I've used (e.g. `oh-my-zsh`, `pure`)

> I would have assumed needing to resource `zshrc` because you needed to change some config isn't that uncommon?

Honestly I don't know, because I won't do that myself. As I said above:

> Most likely you should put them (excluding Starship initialization, of course) into a function and execute that instead.

If you really want to re-source `.zshrc`, I would suggest guarding everything or else one day they are going to cause troubles like this issue.

Look at your config, do you realize your `PATH` are going longer and longer with each source?

Also, you are sourcing many other plugins like `z.sh` and `up.sh` as well, what if they don't include some sort of guard and blows everything? Not to mention it is slow too.

---

> Is there some way to maybe wrap `eval "$(starship init zsh)"` in a guard so that it isn't called a second time?

```sh
if ! typeset -f starship_precmd > /dev/null; then
    eval "$(starship init zsh)"
fi
```

Starship defines many other functions, here `starship_precmd` is just a example and you are welcome to something else.

---

> I would say that it is a bug with starship, because I've never had this issue with any other prompt that I've used (e.g. `oh-my-zsh`, `pure`)

I would assume those use zsh's builtin `prompt` function so they are essentially not loaded twice. Unfortunately this is not possible since Starship is not a zsh-only prompt and can't utilize zsh in the same way.

Wow thanks for the detailed response! That's awesome!

> Look at your config, do you realize your PATH are going longer and longer with each source?
> Also, you are sourcing many other plugins like z.sh and up.sh as well, what if they don't include some sort of guard and blows everything? Not to mention it is slow too.

I never thought about that before, I will think about changing my workflow for how I source changes to my zsh config 👍 

Thanks again :)

I dunno man. I see the same problem here, and this situation is pretty weird and will require a bit of digging around.

There is a one second wait time after you press Escape to enter vim mode that if you type i to re-insert, it will eat a line of history from above. This is testing with a cleared out zshrc and I really didn't set anything else up other than starship and follow a minimal zsh setup from scratch on this Mac. It was this guide I was using: https://scriptingosx.com/2019/07/moving-to-zsh-06-customizing-the-zsh-prompt/

So anyway, I went on to try out [znap](https://github.com/marlonrichert/zsh-snap), and in some issue in there I was given this to init starship inside:

```
znap eval starship 'starship init zsh --print-full-init'
prompt_starship_precmd
znap prompt

znap source zsh-users/zsh-autosuggestions
```

For whatever reason with this setup instead of `eval "$(starship init zsh)"`, the broken behavior of eating history is now gone. 

I was also able to confirm that only if I leave in `znap source zsh-users/zsh-autosuggestions` the correct behavior stays.

- the use of znap did not fix this issue
- autosuggestions maybe has something in it that undoes some problematic setting that starship *might* be doing. I think it may be related to having a two line status line.
- using `jeffreytse/zsh-vi-mode` with znap results in a disappeared cursor and even more lines being eaten. Totally broken it seems.
